title: vectorized-head-tiler-and-kv-aging-groomer-for-low-latency-mistral-llama-qwen
author: Sofia Alvarez
release_notes: Improves latency tail for Mistral/LLama/Qwen by introducing a vectorized head tiler and an adaptive KV ageing/groomer. No API changes. Recommended to enable behind runtime flag in canary before full rollout.
description:
Context and motivation: Production traffic shows intermittent token-level latency spikes for narrow-batch, long-context Mistral and some Llama variants. Root cause analysis found two contributing factors: (1) per-head memory layout causing suboptimal kernel dispatch for multi-query attention (MQA/GQA mixes) on certain sequences, (2) KV cache fragmentation and long-lived cold entries that increase scheduling overhead and reduce effective batch coalescing. Goals: reduce 95/99th percentile token latency without sacrificing throughput; provide a guard-rail rollout path and compatibility across Qwen/Mistral/Llama model quirks.

Design summary: This PR implements two complementary runtime optimizations: 1) Vectorized Head Tiler: a lightweight tiling layer that reorganizes per-head tensors into a contiguous vectorized layout prior to kernel dispatch. The tiler operates at the level of the runtime planning stage and emits a tiling hint used by kernel selector to choose vector-friendly kernels when beneficial. It is conservative by default (enabled for sequences > 512 and when head_count modulo tile_width == 0). 2) Adaptive KV Aging & Groomer: background pass that tracks per-request KV access recency and evicts or compacts KV slabs that are stale, consolidating hot entries and reducing fragmentation. The groomer interacts with the continuous-batching coalescer to avoid coalescing batches containing entries scheduled for eviction in the same window. Together these reduce kernel polymorphism and scheduling churn, improving steady-state latency and tail.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-2158) - [x] Unit tests for tiler and groomer logic - [x] Integration tests in perf-canary harness - [x] Runtime flag gating and telemetry hooks - [x] Canary rollout plan in console feature flags

Commits (high level): - Implement vectorized head tiler and planner hint (S. Alvarez) - Add KV aging tracker and groomer loop with heuristics (S. Alvarez) - Kernel selector updates to respect tiler hints and fallback paths (R. Patel) - Tests and perf harness scenarios (M. Chen) - Docs + rollout notes (E. Morris)

Files changed (high level): - runtime/planner/tiler.cpp (new): tiler implementation and hint emission - runtime/kv/groomer.cpp (new): background grooming loop and heuristics - runtime/kernel_selector/kernels.cpp: respect tiler hints and add vector kernels mapping - runtime/batching/coalescer.cpp: avoid coalescing windows that overlap groomer eviction cycle - tests/perf/tiler_groomer_scenarios.yaml: perf scenarios for canary - docs/runtime/notes/vectorized-tiler.md: rollout and telemetry guidance - examples/benchmarks/mistral-tiler-run.sh: small bench harness - ci/workflows/perf-canary.yml: adds new canary job

Small illustrative diffs: - runtime/planner/tiler.cpp (snippet): "if (seq_len > 512 && head_count % tile_w == 0) planner.emit_hint(Hint::VectorizeHeads, tile_w);" - runtime/kv/groomer.cpp (snippet): "for (auto &slab : slabs) if (slab.last_access < now - groom_window) compact(slab);"

Testing and perf: Unit tests cover tiler hint correctness and groomer eviction safety. Perf canary runs show median token latency unchanged, 95th reduced by ~12% and 99th reduced by ~20% on our Mistral-13B echo workload (narrow batch, long context). Memory overhead in steady state measured at +1.8% due to temporary tiling buffers; groomer reduces long-term KV slab memory by ~4% in realistic chat workloads.

Compatibility and fallbacks: The tiler is advisory — kernel selector may ignore it if vector kernels are not available for a model/arch. Groomer uses conservative thresholds by default and exposes a runtime config for aggressiveness. Both features are gated behind runtime flags: runtime.feature.vectorized_head_tiler and runtime.feature.kv_groomer.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main gated off (this PR leaves flags disabled by default) 2) Canary enable for 5% of traffic on dedicated pools with perf-canary monitoring 3) Gradual ramp to 50% with rollback window 4) Full enable when 2 consecutive weeks of SLOs show improvement or no regressions.

Related: ENG-2158 (design), ENG-2211 (perf regression triage), internal notes: infra/ops incident #INT-708 (token tail investigation).

review_thread: Rajesh Patel: Can we make the tiler fallback faster when vector kernels are absent? Suggest adding a cheap capability probe.
